name: float-operations-decided-by-a-bound-constant-precise
rationale: The rows of sfold_fast compiled without fast math, so no float operation carries a flag, over finite lanes x (-2.5, 2.5, both zeros, 0.5, -0.5, 3, -3), with the additions, subtractions, products and quotients of a NaN constant and x in either place: f[0..3) the zero products, which keep the sign IEEE arithmetic gives them and which a rewrite to +0 would lose, f[3..10) the NaN beside x, f[10..12) the fused multiply-adds, f[12..18) the operations of constants alone, h[0..2) the half zero products, h[2..6) a half NaN beside half4(x) and h[6] its fused multiply-add. Constant 0 is +0 and 1 is -0 (float), 2 a quiet NaN with its sign set and a payload (0xffc12345), 3 a signalling NaN (0x7f800321), 4 and 5 the half zeros and 6 a signalling half NaN with its sign set (0xfd21). The 8 bytes past each record pin the 0xCD fill.

name: manual-float3-fetch-at-an-offset-transformed-onto-three-of-four-pixels
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's manual-vertex-fetch case, whose zero constants gave a degenerate position. Constant 132 enables manual fetch; table slot 0 holds the same-library callback re::vertexfetch::fetchFromFloat3, and record 0 of the vertex-argument buffer (15 records of 24 bytes, the rest null) points at float3 positions with stride 12 and offset 12, which skips a leading decoy vertex (40, 40, 40). The three positions are (-1, -1), (3, -1), (-1, 3) with z = 1/4 with the matrix z scale 2, so world z = 5/8. The instance matrix (objectToCrWorld, column-major) scales x and y by 1/2, scales z and translates by (-1/4, -1/4, 1/8); crWorldToProjArray[0] keeps x, y and w and maps z to z/2 + 1/16, so the clip triangle is (-3/4, -3/4), (5/4, -3/4), (-3/4, 5/4) at w = 1. It covers the pixel centres (-1/2, 1/2), (-1/2, -1/2) and (1/2, -1/2) of the 2x2 target with a margin of at least 1/4 from every edge and misses (1/2, 1/2): pixel (1, 0) keeps its fill. The depth is the same at all three vertices, so its interpolation is exact; every product and sum is a small dyadic value, exact in float with or without contraction, and the observer writes (x + 1/2, y + 1/2, z, 1) for each covered pixel. This entry applies no depth bias (screenSpaceDepthBias = 1/4 is authored but unread): depth 0.375.

name: manual-vertex-fetch-null-buffer-defaults
no_effect: Zero instance and view constants give a degenerate position: the primitive covers no fragment, so the render target keeps its authored bytes.
rationale: Function constant 132 enables manual vertex fetch. Every zero-initialized embedded vertex-buffer pointer is null, so each AIR guard bypasses its table lookup and supplies the defined default attribute. Slot zero is the exact same-library invalid-format callback that supplies the table's required type but is unreachable. Zero transform constants produce a deterministic degenerate position. Buffer 30 and its reflected offset-zero device buffer are now authored explicitly; the invalid-format callback deterministically supplies the same default attribute when that first record is reached. This indexed AIR identity has the same reflected entry/resource/linkage contract and is authored independently.

name: quad-and-or-xor-and-broadcast-first-in-full-quads
rationale: One threadgroup of 64 threads, sixteen full quads. Thread t writes quad_and and quad_or of the int in[t], quad_xor of it as uint, quad_or of it as ushort, quad_xor of it as uchar, and quad_broadcast_first of it as uint. in[t] is 2((37t + 11) mod 257) - 255, odd, so no product is zero; integer products wrap.

name: quad-and-or-xor-and-broadcast-first-in-partial-quads
rationale: Two threadgroups of 42 threads: each ends in a quad of two threads (its simdgroup's lanes 8 and 9 of 10), so the quad operations cover partial quads. Thread t writes quad_and and quad_or of the int in[t], quad_xor of it as uint, quad_or of it as ushort, quad_xor of it as uchar, and quad_broadcast_first of it as uint. in[t] is 2((37t + 11) mod 257) - 255, odd, so no product is zero; integer products wrap.

name: quad-and-or-xor-and-prefix-sum-in-a-fragment-function-over-cut-quads
rationale: Drawn over a 7x5 target: its last column and row are quads the target cuts, whose other pixels lie outside it. Pixel (x, y) holds b = (7x + 13y) xor 0x5a and returns quad_and of b | 0x100, quad_or and quad_xor of b, and its inclusive prefix sum.

name: quad-and-or-xor-and-prefix-sum-in-a-fragment-function-over-full-quads
rationale: Drawn over an 8x8 target, sixteen full quads. Pixel (x, y) holds b = (7x + 13y) xor 0x5a and returns quad_and of b | 0x100, quad_or and quad_xor of b, and its inclusive prefix sum.

name: quad-broadcast-first-in-a-fragment-arm-metal-speculates
rationale: Drawn over an 8x8 target, sixteen full quads. quad_broadcast_first in a branch whose arm joins the other path through a phi. Metal's backend speculates the arm and answers with the quad's lane 0 whether active or not (measured on the M3 Max and the M4); the AIR keeps the call in the branch, and the translation speculates the arm as Metal does (air::canon::speculate). Pixels with (x + 2y) mod 3 nonzero take quad_broadcast_first of x + 64y; the others return -7.

name: quad-broadcast-first-in-an-arm-metal-speculates
rationale: One threadgroup of 64 threads, sixteen full quads. quad_broadcast_first in a branch whose arm joins the other path through a phi. Metal's backend speculates the arm and answers with the quad's lane 0 whether active or not (measured on the M3 Max and the M4); the AIR keeps the call in the branch, and the translation speculates the arm as Metal does (air::canon::speculate). Threads with t mod 3 nonzero take quad_broadcast_first of 10t + 1; the others write 7777.

name: quad-fills-and-rotations-in-full-quads
rationale: One threadgroup of 64 threads, sixteen full quads. Thread t writes the quad fills of in[t] with filling data in[t] + 1000: up by 1, down by 2, up by 1 modulo 2, down by 3 modulo 4, then up and down by buffer 2's (delta, modulo) pairs, down by its first delta with no modulo, quad_shuffle_rotate_up by 1 and by its third word, and the second lane of a float2 fill up by 2. Metal's quad fill is the simdgroup fill within the quad for a modulo of 2 or 4. Buffer 2's pairs are (1, 2), (3, 4), (5, 4) and (1, 4). The inputs are 1, -1, 2, -2, 0.5 and -0.5 (in[t] is the pattern's entry 7t mod 32), so every quad product, sum and prefix of any association order is exact.

name: quad-fills-and-rotations-with-zero-and-whole-segment-deltas
rationale: One threadgroup of 64 threads, sixteen full quads. Thread t writes the quad fills of in[t] with filling data in[t] + 1000: up by 1, down by 2, up by 1 modulo 2, down by 3 modulo 4, then up and down by buffer 2's (delta, modulo) pairs, down by its first delta with no modulo, quad_shuffle_rotate_up by 1 and by its third word, and the second lane of a float2 fill up by 2. Metal's quad fill is the simdgroup fill within the quad for a modulo of 2 or 4. Buffer 2's pairs are (0, 2), (2, 4), (6, 2) and (2, 2): a zero delta, and deltas of a whole segment and more. The inputs are 1, -1, 2, -2, 0.5 and -0.5 (in[t] is the pattern's entry 7t mod 32), so every quad product, sum and prefix of any association order is exact.

name: quad-fills-in-a-fragment-function-over-cut-quads

name: quad-operations-in-a-vertex-function-of-64-points
rationale: Sixty-four rasterization-disabled points, two full simdgroups on Apple GPUs. Vertex v writes the quad fill up by 1, the fill down by buffer 2's pair (1, 2), quad_shuffle_rotate_up by 1, quad_broadcast_first, quad_product, the exclusive prefix sum and the inclusive prefix product of in[v], and quad_and of v | 2^30 xor quad_xor of v. name: quad-operations-on-every-mask-of-active-lanes
rationale: One threadgroup of 64 threads, sixteen full quads. Quad k (threads 4k to 4k + 3 of the grid) runs the operations on the lanes of the mask k mod 16 alone, in an arm of six stores: quad_broadcast_first, quad_product, the exclusive prefix sum, the inclusive prefix product, quad_or of t << 8 and quad_xor of t, each with bit 30 set so their words are normal floats; the others keep -7. The inputs are 1, -1, 2, -2, 0.5 and -0.5 (in[t] is the pattern's entry 7t mod 32), so every quad product, sum and prefix of any association order is exact.

rationale: Drawn over an 8x8 target, sixteen full quads. Pixel (x, y) holds the pattern 1, -1, 2, -2, 0.5, -0.5 at (3x + 5y) mod 6, so every quad product and prefix is exact. Pixels with (x + 2y) mod 3 nonzero return quad_product, the exclusive prefix sum, the inclusive prefix product and quad_or of x << 8 over the pixels the branch takes; the others return -7.

The inputs are 1, -1, 2, -2, 0.5 and -0.5 (in[t] is the pattern's entry 7t mod 32), so every quad product, sum and prefix of any association order is exact.

Each pixel returns quad_product, the exclusive prefix sum and the inclusive prefix product of its value, and quad_broadcast_first of x + 64y.

The inputs are 1, -1, 2, -2, 0.5 and -0.5 (in[t] is the pattern's entry 7t mod 32), so every quad product, sum and prefix of any association order is exact.

rationale: Forty-two rasterization-disabled points: a full simdgroup and one of ten vertices, whose last quad holds two. rationale: Drawn over a 7x5 target: its last column and row are quads the target cuts, whose other pixels lie outside it. Pixel (x, y) holds x + 64y and filling data 10000 more; Each pixel returns simd_shuffle_and_fill_up by 1, simd_shuffle_and_fill_down by 3, the fill up by 2 modulo 8 and the fill down by 5 modulo 16, over the pixels Metal packs into its simdgroup.

name: simdgroup-fills-in-a-fragment-function-over-full-quads

Pixel (x, y) holds x + 64y and filling data 10000 more; Each pixel returns simd_shuffle_and_fill_up by 1, simd_shuffle_and_fill_down by 3, the fill up by 2 modulo 8 and the fill down by 5 modulo 16, over the pixels Metal packs into its simdgroup.

name: linked-k24-gather-qvm-n-float
rationale: Reaching variant of linked-zero-k cases of this entry, whose parameters stop the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes; the user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). The parameters select N = 32 outputs (one threadgroup's 32 columns) over K = 24 rows: the guard (threadgroup_position.y << 5) < N passes, lanes 0 to 23 each dequantize one 8-bit row of W (row stride N bytes) and scale it, the simdgroup sums the 32 partial results, and lane 0 hands all 32 to the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at element indices 0 to 31 (128 bytes, observed whole). x holds 1, 2, 3 repeating, the scales 0.5, 1, 2 repeating, the biases 0 to 3 repeating, and W small integers below 16, so every product and partial sum is an integer multiple of 0.5 far below 2^24: exact in any order or contraction.

name: linked-zero-k-gather-qvm-n-float
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: A single invocation and unit gather batch select literal index zero from the authored buffers. The quantized K extent and vector-row count are zero while the quantization group size is one, making every accumulation and final postfix loop zero-trip and leaving the sole bounded destination element unchanged. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: draw-bases-of-a-draw-from-vertex-start-0xfffffffa-and-base-instance-7
rationale: Four rasterization-disabled points from vertexStart 0xfffffffa, two instances from baseInstance 7. Vertex vid of instance iid writes (vid, iid, [[base_vertex]], [[base_instance]]) to out[(iid % 4) * 8 + vid % 8]: Metal's base vertex of a draw without an index buffer is its vertexStart, so every vertex reads 0xfffffffa and its vertex_id runs 0xfffffffa to 0xfffffffd; the instance_id runs 7 and 8 and the base instance is 7. Slots no vertex writes keep the 0xab fill.

name: draw-bases-of-an-indexed-draw-with-base-vertex-minus-3-and-base-instance-2
rationale: Four rasterization-disabled points of the 16-bit indices 5 to 8 under baseVertex -3, two instances from baseInstance 2. Vertex vid of instance iid writes (vid, iid, [[base_vertex]], [[base_instance]]) to out[(iid % 4) * 8 + vid % 8]: Metal's base vertex of an indexed draw is its baseVertex, so every vertex reads 0xfffffffd (-3 as a uint) and its vertex_id is the index plus -3, 2 to 5; the instance_id runs 2 and 3 and the base instance is 2. Slots no vertex writes keep the 0xab fill.

name: ushort-draw-bases-of-a-draw-from-vertex-start-0xfffffffa-and-base-instance-0x10007
rationale: Four rasterization-disabled points from vertexStart 0xfffffffa, two instances from baseInstance 0x10007, read as ushort [[base_vertex]] and [[base_instance]]. Vertex vid of instance iid writes (vid, iid, base_vertex, base_instance) to out[(iid % 4) * 8 + vid % 8]: the ushort bases are the low 16 bits, 0xfffa and 7, while the uint vertex_id runs 0xfffffffa to 0xfffffffd and the instance_id 0x10007 and 0x10008. Slots no vertex writes keep the 0xab fill.

name: ushort-draw-bases-of-a-uint32-indexed-draw-with-base-vertex-minus-3-and-base-instance-2
rationale: Four rasterization-disabled points of the 32-bit indices 5 to 8 under baseVertex -3, two instances from baseInstance 2, read as ushort [[base_vertex]] and [[base_instance]]. Vertex vid of instance iid writes (vid, iid, base_vertex, base_instance) to out[(iid % 4) * 8 + vid % 8]: the ushort base vertex is the low 16 bits of -3, 0xfffd, the base instance 2; the vertex_id is the index plus -3, 2 to 5, and the instance_id runs 2 and 3. Slots no vertex writes keep the 0xab fill.

name: sixteen-overlapping-triangles-update-each-pixel-word-in-raster-order
rationale: Ordering evidence for raster order groups on a device buffer. The draw is 16 instances of the executors' fullscreen triangle on an 8x8 rgba8_unorm target, so sixteen fragments cover every pixel. Each fragment reads the uint word of its pixel (index 8 * uint(position.y) + uint(position.x)) and writes 3v + 1 back with a plain load and store; the word is in raster order group 0, which orders overlapping fragments' accesses, so each pixel's sixteen read-modify-writes run one after another. Word i starts at i, so it ends at 3^16 i + (3^16 - 1) / 2 (mod 2^32; 21523360 for pixel 0, 2733466783 for pixel 63), whatever order the identical fragments take: a lost update (two fragments reading the same value) leaves 3^15 i + (3^15 - 1) / 2 or less, and a pixel-index mix-up shows as the start value of another word. Instances cannot be told apart by the fragment, so this settles the ordering guarantee as mutual exclusion of the read-modify-write, not submission order. The color output is not observed. The AIR has no loop.

name: copy-two-array-slices-with-one-column-past-the-width-guard
rationale:
air.read_texture_2d_array.i16.v4f32 had no authored case; 36 corpus sources sit behind it. The host copies two array slices of one texture into another, guarded by the destination's own queried width and height and by a byte in a 112-byte packed constant struct.

The grid is 5x2 against a 4x3 destination, which exercises both guards from opposite sides: the x=4 column is rejected by the width query, and the y=2 row is never dispatched, so four of the twelve texels in each slice must still hold their poison when the case reads back. Every source texel is a distinct dyadic and the third channel encodes the slice, so a case that read the wrong slice, transposed a coordinate, or copied one slice twice moves a value rather than repeating one.

The flag byte is the last scalar of a packed struct at offset 104, chosen zero so the copy path runs; the other branch writes NaN to both slices, which would be visible immediately. The 384 output bytes were derived by hand; Metal and MoltenVK both answer them.

name: read-a-threadgroup-width-the-pipeline-declares
rationale: The same kernel with `has_width` true: `width` is the ordinary `threads_per_threadgroup` builtin, so every thread of the two threadgroups of two writes 2. The pair with the gate-off case shows the gate, not the builtin, decides what the read is.

name: a-thread-reads-its-own-write-after-a-texture-fence-without-sparseness
rationale: The control of the write case (the case of name what-a-write-to-an-unmapped-texel-of-a-sparse-texture-does): on apple-m3-max-macos26.7 that case's thread read the old value of a mapped texel it had written and fenced, so this case runs the same AIR and probes on a texture that is not sparse, to tell ordering from sparseness. Texture 0 is 256x128 r32_float with texel (x, y) = 1000y + x + 1 (exact), not sparse. Thread i runs probe i of buffer 0 (32 bytes: kind, x, y, 0, then a float4 value) and writes out[2i] = the raw bits of the float4 sparse_read of texel (x, y) and out[2i+1] = (resident() ? 1 : 0, kind, i, 0x5A5); kind 0 first writes the value at (x, y) and fences the texture, kind 1 only reads. Each probe addresses its own texel. Probes: 0 read (5, 7); 1 write 42.5 at (6, 7) and read it; 2 write 43.5 at (200, 7) and read it; 3 read (201, 7), never written; 4 write 44.5 at (256, 7), past the width, and read it; 5 write 45.5 at (127, 127); 6 write 46.5 at (128, 127); 7 write 47.5 at (5, 128), past the height; 8 read (129, 127), beside probe 6's write. The value written is (v, 1, 2, 3) and r32_float keeps v. Texture 0 is an out-of-bounds target of the texture form. The output is pre-filled with 0xAB; the AIR has no loop.

name: what-a-write-to-an-unmapped-texel-of-a-sparse-texture-does
rationale: The first reading: what a write to an unmapped texel of a sparse texture does on Metal, observed by the writing thread itself. The texture is an input (its unmapped texels have no contents to read back after the work), declared read_write by the function, so the oracle makes it with shader read and write usage, and the Vulkan candidate a sparse resident storage image. A sparse texture is made on Metal from a sparse heap of 16 KiB pages and mapped with MTLResourceStateCommandEncoder before the work, and on Vulkan as a sparse resident image bound with vkQueueBindSparse; Only the mapped texels' authored bytes are uploaded. Each region is a whole number of tiles on every device that runs the case (an executor refuses a region that is not whole tiles of its device), so the mapped texels are the same wherever the case runs; each run prints its tiling. Texture 0 is 256x128 r32_float with texel (x, y) = 1000y + x + 1 (exact) and its left 128x128 mapped (x 128..255 unmapped). Thread i runs probe i of buffer 0 (32 bytes: kind, x, y, 0, then a float4 value) and writes out[2i] = the raw bits of the float4 sparse_read of texel (x, y) and out[2i+1] = (resident() ? 1 : 0, kind, i, 0x5A5); kind 0 first writes the value at (x, y) and fences the texture (texture fence: the thread's write is visible to its own later read), kind 1 only reads. Each probe addresses its own texel. Probes: 0 read (5, 7), mapped; 1 write 42.5 at (6, 7), mapped, and read it; 2 write 43.5 at (200, 7), unmapped, and read it; 3 read (201, 7), unmapped, never written; 4 write 44.5 at (256, 7), past the width, and read it; 5 write 45.5 at (127, 127), the last mapped texel of the tile's corner; 6 write 46.5 at (128, 127), the first unmapped one; 7 write 47.5 at (5, 128), past the height; 8 read (129, 127), unmapped, beside probe 6's write. The value written is (v, 1, 2, 3) and r32_float keeps v. Texture 0 is an out-of-bounds target of the texture form. The output is pre-filled with 0xAB; the AIR has no loop.

name: linked-single-unit-average-write-vertical
rationale: Every source, destination, kernel, stride, dilation, threadgroup cube, and group-count extent is exactly one with zero offsets. The required multi-destination constants declare one float source at table element zero and one active float destination at element one, so this pooling variant executes only its unit window and bounded single-lane collective before writing exact one.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-eight
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 28 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-seven linked _uber_clear bodies. A thirty-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; the final selector reads register 2 and writes exact zero to the poisoned primary texel.

name: weighted-average-two-corner-records
rationale: Two loop-free invocations evaluate distinct weighted averages with exactly representable inputs and results: (2+4+6+8)/4 becomes 5, while (3*2)/2 remains 3. Exact comparison proves only the first float of each 32-byte record changes.
